task: Bug: `tenacity.after_log` crashes with `TypeError` when `retry_state.seconds_since_start` is `None` (it is `None` when the outcome timestamp has not been set). The log message should still be emitted, showing "?" in place of the elapsed seconds.
why:
The two candidates make the same fix: both print "?" for the elapsed time when the timestamp is missing, both change only `tenacity/after.py`, and both add one test. Both pass all checks.
c1 won on test quality. Its test checks `assertIsNone(retry_state.seconds_since_start)` before calling the logger, so it would fail if the setup stopped producing `None`. Its explicit `if ... is None` check also matches how `tenacity/stop.py` already handles this property.
c2 is a bit shorter and reads the property only once. Its test never checks that the value really is `None`, so if the setup changed it could pass without testing the bug.
